course_description:
This course provides Dentistry students with an introduction to important concepts in genetics, biological chemistry, and dental tissue engineering that are of particular relevance to future Dentists. It builds on the concepts learned in first year chemistry and applies new concepts to health problems encountered in dental practice.

The 2026 version of DENT2222 has been designed with feedback incorporated from the course coordinator and student feedback from the previous year to ensure an improved student learning experience.

course_aims: DENT2222 aims to familiarise Dentistry students with the basics of genetics, biological chemistry, and dental tissue engineering and apply this to oral and systemic diseases and clinical situations. Students will also get an introduction to the tissue engineering used to treat oral disease.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the impact of nutritional status and endocrine disorders on oral health and disease relevant to dentistry.
Explain the effects and interactions of key medications on oral health and their relevance to dental care.
Understand the role played by genetic, cellular, and molecular abnormalities on oral cancer and orofacial clefts.
Appreciate specific molecular mechanisms that regulate wound healing, tissue repair and tissue regeneration in dental therapies.
Describe dental tissue engineering and advances in materials and scaffolds.
Develop skills and attributes of collaborative teamwork.

assessment_details.task_description: A major focus of this course is to develop students’ understanding of how systemic medications and drug interactions influence oral health and dental treatment. This includes recognising interactions relevant to dental conditions and systemic diseases with oral manifestations. As part of this assessment, students will work in teams of four to investigate a selected drug or drug interaction relevant to dental practice. Students are expected to collaboratively research, analyse, and critically evaluate the literature to understand the underlying biological mechanisms and clinical relevance. The project will be presented as a 4‑minute video presentation on an infographic poster developed by the team. The video presentation on the infographic poster must be submitted on or before the due date. Students should focus on the mechanism of drug action and interaction, oral and systemic relevance, risk mitigation and patient safety, and clinical implications for dental care. Students are expected to contribute effectively as a team and demonstrate clear communication of scientific concepts in a clinically relevant manner. The assessment will be marked according to published criteria available on Blackboard, and all submissions must be completed and submitted by the due date.
